audit.why: 52.47% over 465 games supports EVEN at 5.5/10, with level 2 the one genuinely even stage: Nevermove reaches 850 — the same as Noxious Blast — and roots on its return, which is the only way Swain starts a fight on Cassiopeia.
audit.corrected: Rating unchanged; the stages now hang on Nevermove's return-root and the 650 drain radius.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0], [2], [3], [4] and [6].side read Skill while content win[] read Cassiopeia on all five — five rows rendering two different answers.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer (Cassiopeia, Skill, then Cassiopeia through) and the win rate agrees.
audit.corrected: Those five sides moved to Cassiopeia with each why rewritten in the same proposal. Rows 1 and 5 already agreed. No win[N] edits needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page described Swain's ultimate as 'his drain mode' with no radius and no cooldown, never mentioned that Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass, and attributed the pull to his Q ('his root-E into Q pull').
audit.why: Nevermove (E), 850 range on 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, launches a wave that roots on the way back to him, and the recast pulls rooted champions closer — the pull is on E, not Q. Death's Hand (Q), 750 on 7/6/5/4/3s, does more damage per bolt that hits, so distance reduces it. Vision of Empire (W) is 5500-7500 range on 22-18s and slows and reveals. Demonic Ascension (R) is a flat 120s and drains inside 650, sustaining indefinitely while it has champions to drain — the counterplay is the circle, not the cast. Ravenous Flock (P) heals him and permanently grows his max health, which is what makes Grievous Wounds a core purchase rather than a situational one.
audit.corrected: Return-root, the E recast pull, the 650 radius and the anti-heal requirement written across the chart, cooldowns, spikes and the content prose.

audit.why: It is the field that carries the numbers.
audit.corrected: Nevermove 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s at 850, Demonic Ascension flat 120s at 650, Death's Hand 7s to 3s at 750.

audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals off soul fragments and permanently raises his maximum health, and Demonic Ascension sustains for as long as it has a champion inside 650. Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal now stated as a core item with the reason, in breakdown.carry, ahead and spikes[2].

audit.why: His E is Nevermove; Twin Fang deals increased damage to poisoned targets and heals Cassiopeia, with no execute component in Riot's text.
audit.corrected: Both replaced with the real mechanics.

notes: Both packet.suspectNames entries are FALSE POSITIVES — 'Save Petrifying Gaze' and 'Use Demonic Ascension' are exact names — but wants.you[2] was still wrong for another reason: it called Demonic Ascension a channel. Riot's text describes a form that persists as long as he is draining a champion, not a channel a stun interrupts, so I rewrote it around the Nevermove pull instead and left wants.foe[1] alone. The two genuinely fabricated names were in the content layer and are fixed: 'Torment of the Roots' (spikes[1]) is not a Swain ability, and 'Twin Fang execute' (spikes[2]) is not a Cassiopeia mechanic. Five chart rows disagreed across layers and were moved to the content layer and packet. One flag I did NOT write from: Ravenous Flock carries a derived percentHealth flag and _missing suggests he 'bypasses stacking resistances'. Riot's description says only that his ravens collect soul fragments that heal him and raise his maximum health, so per the brief I trusted the description and made no resistance claim.
